author: delegate-eval
title: Refuse a pasted agenda that is for another meeting, and say so
body:
## What

When an official pastes an agenda link or uploads a packet, the briefing run now checks that the document is for the meeting they chose. If the packet's own date says it is for a different meeting, no briefing is published, the meeting reads "Agenda is for a different meeting (dated ...)", and the official can try another link. A discovered agenda whose stated date is off is logged, not refused.

Builds on the availability gate in #2478, merged 2026-10-06.

## Why

The second half of the reported incident. After a briefing was published without the agenda, the official's only way out was to paste the right link into the next meeting's slot. That filed the agenda under the wrong date, and nothing on the page said so.

The availability gate cannot catch a real agenda for the wrong meeting: the agent read a complete packet and says so, honestly. Only the date the document itself states can. The pasted-link path is where this happens, because the official picks the slot and the system takes the document on trust.

Ticket: [Fix briefings marked ready with no agenda packet](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2azeac).

## How

- The artifact gains two fields, `packet_stated_meeting_date` and `packet_date_verification`, recorded on every run: the date the agenda document states on its cover or header, and whether it matched the dispatch target within three days, mismatched, or could not be read.
- For a pasted or uploaded packet, `assessPublishability` refuses the row when the stated date is more than three days from the slot the official chose, or the agent reports a mismatch. The comparison is against the dispatch target, not the artifact's own `meeting_date`: the agent writes both, so an agent that copied the packet's date into `meeting_date` would make a wrong-meeting packet look dated right (Bugbot's finding on the first version). Three days lets holiday shifts of a day or two pass. It also refuses when no upload row exists for this run, so a user-provided artifact cannot publish into a slot nobody submitted into. The upload row is found by the dispatch date, because the artifact's echoed date has not always matched it.
- For a discovered agenda the same condition is logged as a warning and the row publishes. In the review, date heuristics refused good briefings and missed misleading ones, and there is no data yet on agent-reported dates. The warning rate after deploy decides whether the follow-up promotes it to a refusal.
- The refusal reason is stored on the upload row (one nullable column, one migration). The meetings list reports the row as `rejected` with the reason, and the status pill turns it into words. A fresh submission clears the reason so the row reads as processing again.
- The QA gate mirrors the check: an error on a user-provided run, a warning on a discovered one.

## What this affects

- Only pasted and uploaded agendas can be refused by this change. Discovered agendas are unchanged apart from a log line.
- The Briefings page: one new status label on the awaiting-agenda row and the upcoming card. No change to the detail page.
- The meeting_briefing experiment: two new optional fields.
- The gp-api generated agent-job contracts file is regenerated, and the background comparability digest for this agent is re-pinned, as that test requires when the manifest or instruction change. The web app's copy of the contracts is left alone because nothing in the web app reads these fields.
- Unaffected: briefings already written, the chief of staff chat, dashboard cards, the hint and schedule tables.

## Testing

- [x] `meetingBriefings.service.test.ts`: upload row found by the dispatch date when the artifact echoes a different day; missing row, another run's row, and a row with neither link nor file refused; two weeks off refused with the reason recorded; a packet for another meeting refused even when the artifact echoes the packet's date; an agent-reported mismatch refused even without a readable date; one day off, an unreadable date, and a malformed date all publish; a discovered agenda with a mismatch publishes.
- [x] `userAgendaUpload.controller.test.ts`: the meetings list reports rejected with the reason. `AgendaStatusPill.test.tsx`: the new labels.
- [x] `test_meeting_briefing_validator.py`: the date check as an error on user-provided runs and a warning on discovered ones.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, prettier, and eslint clean in gp-api and gp-webapp (the web app's only type errors are the `PageProps` global Next generates at build time). Full `npm run verify` left to CI.
